title: 2026-10-22_TeamTNT_Hildegard_Backdoor_Investigation_652
description: Investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The target network has been compromised by the TeamTNT malware family, specifically the Hildegard backdoor. This malware is known to establish command and control (C2) connections using a tmate reverse shell and an Internet Relay Chat (IRC) channel. It also uses process disguise, library injection, and payload encryption to evade detection.

Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: trainee, Password: trainee. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: trainee, Password: trainee. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Users have reported slow performance on the target host. Investigate the host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service in this case is `bioset.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: To determine how the service is automatically started, you can use the `systemctl status bioset.service` command. This will show you the service's configuration and how it is set to start automatically.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for communication, you can use the `ss -tulnp` command. This will show you the network connections and listen ports. The port used for C2 communication in this case is 4444.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check network connections and listen ports.
